messages.content: Can you fetch the server's response if I send a GET request to 'https://api.intent.com/query' with the following queries to recognize their corresponding intents: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there]? The list of intent-codes is [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye].

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the server's response. This is typically used for API calls and web content fetching. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. Must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS endpoint, such as 'https://api.example.com/data'.

intents.description: A list of intent codes derived from user queries, represented as strings. For example, ['weather', 'news'].

timeout.description: The maximum time, in seconds, to wait for the server's response before the request times out. For example, a timeout of 30.0 seconds. This is a float type value.

User-Agent.description: The User-Agent header's value representing the client software identity, such as 'MyApp/1.0'.

Accept.description: The Accept header's value indicating the media types which are acceptable for the response, like 'application/json'.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers to include in the request. If not provided, default headers will be used.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to fetch server's response by sending a GET request to 'https://api.intent.com/query' with queries: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there] and list of intent-codes: [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye].

We need to use the function get_response. Provide the URL, intents, maybe queries? The function signature: get_response takes url, intents (optional), timeout, headers. There's no parameter for queries. But we can pass queries as part of headers? Or maybe we need to encode them in the URL? The user didn't specify how to send queries. We might need to construct query parameters. The function signature doesn't allow queries. But we can embed them in the URL as query string: e.g., https://api.intent.com/query?queries=hello,I want to transfer funds,... But the function signature only has url. So we can modify the URL accordingly.

Thus we should call get_response with url: 'https://api.intent.com/query?queries=hello,I%20want%20to%20transfer%20funds,show%20my%20balance,hey%20there&intent_codes=get_balance,transfer_funds,hello,goodbye'.

But the function signature expects intents: string[]. That might be the intent codes. So we can pass intents: ['get_balance','transfer_funds','hello','goodbye']. The queries are not part of the function signature. So we need to encode them in the URL.

Thus we call:

{
  "url": "https://api.intent.com/query?queries=hello,I%20want%20to%20transfer%20funds,show%20my%20balance,hey%20there",
  "intents": ["get_balance","transfer_funds","hello","goodbye"]
}

We can also set headers if needed. But default is fine.

Thus we produce a function call.
